population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 7 bought the HKD 52 member fare and 25 declined. Most declines (18) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within basic-fare budget, which is an inventory/budget-fit issue rather than a stated price objection. The remaining 7 declines cited low destination appeal, low trip interest, recent travel or a preferred outside option, not fare level. Buyers repeatedly called 52 a bargain, though several said they would not pay the 65 regular fare. Current price sits at the permitted cap of 52, so no higher test is possible.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 52 fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly one-fifth weighted conversion; if a paired fresh sample shows materially lower conversion with unchanged inventory, the bargain framing rather than fare level drives purchases.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 8 bought at the HKD 43 member fare and 24 declined. Most declines (18) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within budget, not a price objection. Six declines cited low trip interest, destination appeal or a recent trip, i.e. optional-trip motivation, not fare. Buyers repeatedly called HKD 43 a bargain and several would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. The current fare sits below the HKD 52 cap, so a higher-fare test is permitted.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will not reduce basic-ticket receipts versus HKD 43, because buyers describe the fare as well below their stated ceilings and several would still buy at the regular fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 36, 15 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain that converted browsing into optional trips; most said they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and eight were low-interest or free-time preferences rather than price objections. No customer rejected the fare as too expensive. The current fare sits well below the HKD 52 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough member purchases that basic ticket receipts per customer meet or exceed those at HKD 36, since no buyer cited price as a barrier and most named the fare a bargain.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 30, 22 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain that turned browsing into an optional trip; most said they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Five declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and five were low-interest optional-leisure declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to strong conversion at the current low fare, but buying at HKD 30 does not establish willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will show that conversion falls enough to reduce total basic-ticket receipts compared with HKD 30, because most current buyers describe the low fare itself as the decisive trigger.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 29, 16 of 32 members bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain; 16 declined, but 12 of those declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections. Only 3 declines reflected low interest or optional-trip appeal, and 1 was a low-interest browse. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current fare sits well below the HKD 52 cap, and buyers repeatedly said they would refuse the HKD 65 normal fare.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts, because current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well under their stated budgets and no decline was a price objection.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 30, 20 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain; most said they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Eight declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and four were low-interest or low-appeal optional-trip refusals despite the cheap fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to strong price sensitivity, but buying at HKD 30 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket fare, so basic receipts stay at or above the HKD 30 baseline.

analysis.summary: At HKD 30, 24 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing the low price as the decisive trigger; several said they would decline at the HKD 65 regular fare. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and four were low-interest or recent-trip objections where price was not the barrier. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to strong price-driven conversion at the current fare, but buying at HKD 30 does not establish willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce conversion enough that basic ticket receipts do not increase, because most current buyers explicitly cite the low fare as the trigger and reject the regular fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 32, 17 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain that converted casual browsing into a trip; most would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Ten declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and five were low-interest or recent-travel objections where price was not the barrier. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to the low fare driving conversion, but buying at HKD 32 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce member conversion enough that basic ticket receipts fall below those at HKD 32, because most current buyers explicitly say they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 31 member fare, 17 of 32 customers bought, all citing the low fare as the decisive trigger; several explicitly said they would decline at HKD 65. Nine declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and six were low-interest optional-leisure declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. This supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at HKD 31 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare above HKD 31 on fresh paired customers will retain enough buyers that basic ticket receipts do not fall, because most purchases were driven by fare attractiveness rather than fixed budgets.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 32, 17 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain well below their budgets; most said they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Nine declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and six were low-interest optional-leisure declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at HKD 32 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare above HKD 32 on fresh paired customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, since most buyers cited large budget headroom and no price objection appeared.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 30, 16 of 32 members bought, citing the low fare as the trigger for optional trips; all said they would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Twelve declines were inventory/budget-forced, not price objections, and four were low-interest or recent-travel choices. No customer objected to the fare itself. The current fare sits well below the HKD 52 cap, and paired metrics suggest higher fares sharply reduce conversion, though that comparison is untested on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce member conversion enough that basic-ticket receipts fall below those at the current low fare, because buyers repeatedly cite the low price itself as the purchase trigger.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 31 member fare, 24 of 32 customers bought, nearly all citing the low fare as the decisive trigger; most would decline the HKD 65 regular fare. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced, and four were low-interest or recent-travel objections rather than price objections. The fare sits well below the HKD 52 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases that basic ticket receipts exceed those at HKD 31, since most current buyers cite the bargain as decisive but many budgets sit well above the current fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 52 HKD is a genuinely low basic fare, and as a frequent bargain hunter I would happily take this optional short trip to a destination with medium appeal. analysis.summary: At the current HKD 32 member fare, 16 of 32 customers bought and 16 declined. Most buyers cite the low fare as the decisive trigger, often despite low destination interest, and many say they would not pay the HKD 65 regular fare. Declines split between low-interest optional leisure and budget/inventory constraints. No customer raised price as a reason to decline. The fare sits well below the HKD 52 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the current HKD 32 baseline, since buyers cite the fare as compelling and no decline cites price.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the HKD 32 member fare, 19 of 32 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain; 13 declined, of whom 8 were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget) and 5 cited low interest or destination appeal rather than price. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current price is below the HKD 52 cap, and several buyers said they would not pay the HKD 65 regular fare, indicating the low fare is doing real work.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because most buyers cite the fare as compelling and no decline was a price objection.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
